title: Lokesh Kanagaraj's DC Crosses Rs 100 Crore Worldwide in Debut Acting Milestone
excerpt: The Tamil filmmaker's first acting role hits Rs 100 crore globally in two weeks, making Wamiqa Gabbi a rare star with two century-grossers in a single year.
body:
• DC, directed by Arun Matheswaran and starring Lokesh Kanagaraj in his acting debut, has crossed Rs 100 crore worldwide within two weeks of its August 7 release.
  • The film earned Rs 61.54 crore net in India and Rs 21.85 crore from international markets by Day 14, according to trade tracker Sacnilk.
  • Co-star Wamiqa Gabbi is on track to become one of the few Indian actresses with two Rs 100 crore grossers in a single calendar year.
  • DC is now the fourth highest-grossing Tamil film of 2026, trailing only Vijay's Jana Nayagan, Suriya's Karuppu, and Vishwanath And Sons.

A Director Steps in Front of the Camera

Lokesh Kanagaraj, the filmmaker behind Tamil blockbusters Vikram, Kaithi, Master and Leo, has carried his box-office track record from the director's chair to the screen. His acting debut DC, directed by Arun Matheswaran and produced by Sun Pictures, crossed the Rs 100 crore mark globally in just 14 days.

The action thriller opened at Rs 4.40 crore net in India on its first day before climbing to Rs 7 crore on Saturday and Rs 9.55 crore on Sunday. A rare day-four uptick — Rs 6 crore, higher than the opening day — signalled strong word-of-mouth was driving repeat viewership. By the end of its second week, the film had accumulated Rs 61.54 crore net domestically with an additional Rs 21.85 crore from overseas markets.

Sun Pictures announced the milestone on social media with a poster declaring "Massive Blockbuster — 100+ Crores Worldwide Gross." Lokesh reshared the post, writing: "All this love… forever grateful."

A Modern Retelling of Devdas

DC is a bloody, A-rated reimagining of Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay's 1917 novel Devdas. Lokesh plays Das, an alcoholic gangster who joins forces with a sex worker named Chandra, played by Wamiqa Gabbi, to wage war against corrupt police officers responsible for killing a bar singer, Parvathy, played by Sanjana Krishnamoorthy.

The film received praise for Lokesh's understated screen presence, Matheswaran's taut direction, and Anirudh Ravichander's 15-track score. Cinema Express noted that DC is "Arun's most accessible, entertaining, and engaging film, and it gives Lokesh Kanagaraj the safest acting debut."

"Lokesh is given this brooding, alcohol-friendly role where his fists and weapons do most of the talking. But he is quite effective in the quieter moments."

— Cinema Express

Wamiqa Gabbi's Breakout Year

DC's century marks a significant milestone for co-star Wamiqa Gabbi. She appeared earlier this year in Baby John, which also crossed the Rs 100 crore mark, making her one of the rare Indian actresses to feature in two century-grossing films in a single year. Gabbi celebrated the milestone on her Instagram Stories with a simple "Thank you."

Industry heavyweights including Suriya, Mahesh Babu, Allu Arjun and Soundarya Rajinikanth have publicly praised the film. Allu Arjun called DC "a Tamil classic," while Mahesh Babu described it as "an original and outstanding film."

Where DC Stands in 2026's Tamil Box Office

Among Tamil releases this year, DC currently ranks fourth in worldwide gross, behind Vijay's Jana Nayagan, Suriya's Karuppu and Vishwanath And Sons. Despite being produced on a medium budget, its strong hold through the weekdays — a rarity for south Indian mass films that tend to be front-loaded — suggests continued earnings as it enters its third week.

The film was distributed in Hindi by Karan Johar's Dharma Productions, though the Hindi version's Rs 0.25 crore daily average suggests limited crossover. The Tamil and Telugu versions have driven the bulk of domestic collections.

What's Next

As DC enters its third week, industry observers are watching whether it can sustain momentum against competition from new releases. An OTT release date has not been announced. Lokesh Kanagaraj's next directorial project remains unconfirmed, though his name continues to be linked to the expanding LCU (Lokesh Cinematic Universe).
